meta.titre: Lenses and image formation: the lens formula, magnification and power

sections.contenu_markdown: A pair of reading glasses from a market stall in Bafoussam, a camera phone in the hand of a student and a projector in a school hall all rely on thin lenses. In each case a lens takes light from an object and forms an image whose position, size and nature depend on how far the object is from the lens. The GCE examiners usually give a focal length and an object distance and ask you to describe the image, so you need the lens formula, the sign convention and the vocabulary (real or virtual, upright or inverted, magnified or diminished). Getting the sign of the image distance right is the key to the answer.

items: Light travels in straight lines and is refracted at the boundary between two media.
A converging lens brings parallel rays to a real focus at the focal point; the focal length $f$ is measured from the lens.
A real image can be formed on a screen; a virtual image cannot, because the rays only appear to come from it.
Lengths in the lens formula must all be in the same unit, such as centimetres.

sections.titre: The lens formula, magnification and power of thin lenses

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question gives a negative focal length or mentions a concave lens.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Insert $f$ as a negative number. For $f = -15\ \mathrm{cm}$ and a real object, the formula $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u}$ always gives a negative $v$, which means a virtual image on the same side as the object, closer to the lens than the object. A negative $v$ must never be dropped when using $m = |v/u|$; the sign tells you the image is virtual, while the magnitude gives the size.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how to measure the focal length from several readings of $u$ and $v$.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Rearranging, $\dfrac{1}{v} = -\dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{f}$. A graph of $\dfrac{1}{v}$ (vertical) against $\dfrac{1}{u}$ (horizontal) is a straight line of gradient $-1$, with both intercepts equal to $\dfrac{1}{f}$. A second method is to plot $uv$ against $u + v$, a line through the origin with gradient $f$ (since $uv = f(u + v)$).

sections.contenu_markdown:
For a thin lens, with object distance $u$, image distance $v$ and focal length $f$, all measured from the lens, the **lens formula** is

$$\frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f}$$

Use the **real-is-positive convention**: $u$ is positive for a real object; $v$ is positive for a **real** image (on the opposite side of the lens from the object) and **negative** for a **virtual** image (same side as the object); $f$ is positive for a **converging** lens and negative for a **diverging** lens. The **linear magnification** is

$$m = \frac{h_i}{h_o} = \left|\frac{v}{u}\right|$$

where $h_i$ and $h_o$ are image and object heights. Real images are inverted; virtual images are upright.

The **power** of a lens is $P = 1/f$, with $f$ in metres, and is measured in dioptres ($\mathrm{m^{-1}}$). For thin lenses in contact the powers add: $P = P_1 + P_2$, so $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$.

**Images in a converging lens** (focal length $f$):

| Object distance | Image |
|---|---|
| $u > 2f$ | real, inverted, diminished, between $f$ and $2f$ |
| $u = 2f$ | real, inverted, same size, at $2f$ |
| $f < u < 2f$ | real, inverted, magnified, beyond $2f$ |
| $u = f$ | image at infinity |
| $u < f$ | virtual, upright, magnified, same side as the object |

A magnifying glass is a converging lens used with the object **inside** the focal length. A **diverging** lens always gives a virtual, upright, diminished image, whatever the object distance.

sections.enonce_markdown: An object $4.5\ \mathrm{cm}$ tall stands $30.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ from a thin converging lens of focal length $12.0\ \mathrm{cm}$. Find the position, nature and height of the image. Then the object is moved to $8.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the lens; describe the new image.
sections.conclusion_markdown: At $30.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ the image is real, inverted, $3.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ tall and $20.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the lens. At $8.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ the image is virtual (negative $v$), upright, three times the size of the object and $24.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the lens on the same side as the object, as in a magnifying glass.

items.pourquoi_faux: In the real-is-positive convention a converging lens has positive $f$ and a diverging lens negative $f$.
items.erreur_markdown: Using $f$ as negative for a converging lens, or positive for a diverging lens.
items.correction_markdown: Decide the sign of $f$ from the type of lens before substituting.

items.pourquoi_faux: The lens formula is $\dfrac1u + \dfrac1v = \dfrac1f$, so $v = \dfrac{uf}{u - f}$; a sign error moves the image to the wrong place.
items.correction_markdown: Start from $\dfrac1v = \dfrac1f - \dfrac1u$ and carry out the subtraction carefully.

items.pourquoi_faux: The formula gives the reciprocal. It must be inverted to obtain the distance.
A negative $v$ is a valid result: it means a virtual image on the same side as the object.
items.erreur_markdown: Stating that a negative image distance means the calculation is wrong.
items.correction_markdown: State 'virtual and upright', and use the magnitude of $v$ for the distance and the size.

items.pourquoi_faux: Power in dioptres needs $f$ in metres.
items.erreur_markdown: Calculating power from $f$ in centimetres, so that $f = 25\ \mathrm{cm}$ gives $P = 0.04\ \mathrm{D}$.

items.enonce_markdown: A converging lens has a focal length of $20.0\ \mathrm{cm}$. An object is placed $60.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ from it. Calculate the image distance and the magnification, and describe the image.
items.solution_markdown: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20.0} - \dfrac{1}{60.0} = \dfrac{3 - 1}{60.0} = \dfrac{2}{60.0}$, so $v = $ **$30.0\ \mathrm{cm}$** (positive, real). $m = \dfrac{30.0}{60.0} = $ **$0.50$**. The image is **real, inverted and diminished**, as expected for $u > 2f$.

items.enonce_markdown: A diverging lens has focal length $-15.0\ \mathrm{cm}$. An object $6.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ tall is placed $45.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the lens. Find the position, nature and height of the image.
items.solution_markdown: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{15.0} - \dfrac{1}{45.0} = -\dfrac{3 + 1}{45.0} = -\dfrac{4}{45.0}$, so $v = $ **$-11.3\ \mathrm{cm}$** (11.25 cm). The negative sign means a **virtual** image on the same side as the object, upright. $m = \dfrac{11.25}{45.0} = 0.25$, so the image height is $0.25 \times 6.0 = $ **$1.5\ \mathrm{cm}$**.

items.enonce_markdown: A thin converging lens of focal length $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ is placed in contact with a thin diverging lens of focal length $-100\ \mathrm{cm}$. Calculate (a) the power and focal length of the combination, and (b) the position and magnification of the image of an object placed $50.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ in front of the combination.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $P_1 = \dfrac{1}{0.25} = +4.0\ \mathrm{D}$ and $P_2 = \dfrac{1}{-1.0} = -1.0\ \mathrm{D}$. For lenses in contact $P = P_1 + P_2 = $ **$3.0\ \mathrm{D}$**, so $f = \dfrac{1}{3.0} = $ **$0.33\ \mathrm{m}$** ($33\ \mathrm{cm}$, a converging combination). (b) With $u = 0.50\ \mathrm{m}$: $\dfrac{1}{v} = P - \dfrac{1}{u} = 3.0 - 2.0 = 1.0\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}$, so $v = $ **$1.0\ \mathrm{m}$** (real, on the far side). The magnification is $m = \dfrac{1.0}{0.50} = $ **$2.0$**, and the image is real, inverted and magnified.

items_markdown: Lens formula: $\dfrac1u + \dfrac1v = \dfrac1f$ with the real-is-positive convention: $f > 0$ for converging lenses, $f < 0$ for diverging ones, $v < 0$ for virtual images.
Linear magnification $m = h_i/h_o = |v/u|$; real images are inverted, virtual images are upright.
Converging lens: object beyond $2f$ gives a real, inverted, diminished image; between $f$ and $2f$ gives real, inverted, magnified; inside $f$ gives virtual, upright, magnified.
A diverging lens always forms a virtual, upright, diminished image.
Power $P = 1/f$ (f in metres) in dioptres; for thin lenses in contact $P = P_1 + P_2$.
Always invert $1/v$ to get $v$, and keep all distances in one unit.
